title: Short vowels: fatha, damma, kasra

bigIdea.text: Arabic writes short vowels as small marks on the letter. A slash on top says 'a', a little curl on top says 'u', a slash underneath says 'i'.

proper.text: Fatha ( َ ) is a small slanted line above the letter: say the letter with a short 'a'. بَ = ba.
Damma ( ُ ) is a small curl like a tiny و above the letter: a short 'u' with rounded lips. بُ = bu.
Kasra ( ِ ) is a small slanted line below the letter: a short 'i'. بِ = bi.
Each of these marks is a haraka ('movement'; plural harakat), and a letter carrying one is called mutaharrik ('moving'). A short vowel lasts one count: short and crisp, never stretched.

Preview: you will also meet ْ (sukun: no vowel), ّ (shadda: a doubled letter) and the doubled marks ً ٌ ٍ (tanween: -an, -un, -in). The next three lessons cover them, and the quiz may already show them.

memoryHook.text: Slash on top 'a', curl on top 'u', slash below 'i'.

extras.text: Persian/Urdu readers: kasra is a clear 'i' (as in 'sit'), not 'e'; damma is 'u' (as in 'put'), not 'o'; fatha is an open 'a', not the 'e' of Persian.
After a heavy letter (such as ص ض ط ظ ق) the vowel sounds deeper and fuller; after a light letter it stays bright. Your letter cards say which letters are heavy.

drills.prompt: Say بَ بُ بِ (ba, bu, bi): short and crisp, one count each.
Now a heavy letter: صَ صُ صِ. Notice the deeper, fuller vowel.
Read across: تَ تُ تِ · ثَ ثُ ثِ · نَ نُ نِ

questions.q: Which mark is a small slanted line ABOVE the letter?
explain: Right: fatha sits on top and says 'a'.
Kasra is the same slash but BELOW the letter.
Damma is a small curl like a tiny و, not a slash.
Sukun is a small round sign meaning no vowel.
Right: the curl on top is a damma, 'u'.
'ba' needs a fatha (a slash on top).
'bi' needs a kasra (a slash below).
No vowel would need a sukun.

options: After the letter, on the line
explain: Right: a small slash under the letter.
Above the letter you find fatha and damma.
Vowel marks sit on the letter, not beside it.
Marks are never written inside a letter.

questions.q: How long is a short vowel (fatha, damma or kasra)?
options: As long as your breath lasts
explain: Right.
Two counts is a long vowel (madd), lesson 22.
Four counts belongs to longer madd types in Stage 2.
Short vowels are never stretched.

options: A short vowel mark: fatha, damma or kasra
A letter that is not pronounced
explain: Right: haraka means 'movement'; the letter moves with a vowel.
Pause signs are different marks (lesson 27).
Harakat are pronounced; they are the vowels.
Long vowels use the letters ا و ي (lesson 22).

questions.q: Which mark looks like a tiny و above the letter?
explain: Right.
Fatha is a straight slash on top.
Kasra is a straight slash below.
Shadda looks like a small 'w' with three points.

questions.q: You see a slash under the letter ت. How do you read it?
explain: Right: a slash below is a kasra, 'i'.
'ta' would need the slash on top (fatha).
'tu' would need a damma curl on top.
No vowel would need a sukun.

questions.q: A Persian/Urdu reader says kasra like the 'e' in 'bed'. What should it be?
explain: Right.
That is closer to a Persian reading of damma, and still wrong for Arabic.
That is closer to fatha.
Kasra is a real vowel.

questions.q: What is a letter that carries a fatha, damma or kasra called?
explain: Right.
Sakin is a letter with sukun (next lesson).
Mushaddad is a letter with shadda (lesson 20).
A letter with a vowel is always pronounced.
Right: kasra under ن.
'na' needs a fatha.
'nu' needs a damma.
'nin' would need two kasras (tanween, lesson 21).

questions.q: What is the best way to say a damma?
options: Round the lips for a short 'u'
explain: Right.
Spread lips make an 'i'-type sound, which belongs to kasra.
A long 'aa' is fatha plus alif, not damma.
Closed lips make ب or م, not a vowel.

questions.q: Which three marks are the short vowels?
explain: Right.
These are other marks, covered in lessons 19–21.
Sukun means no vowel and the maddah means 'stretch'.
Shadda doubles a letter; it is not a vowel.

questions.q: Two letters each carry a kasra, like بِ تِ. How do you read them?
explain: Right: each letter gets a short 'i'.
That would need two fathas.
That would need two dammas.
'bit' would need a sukun on ت instead of a kasra.

remnote: Fatha ( َ ) == Slash above the letter: short 'a' (بَ = ba)
Damma ( ُ ) == Small curl like a tiny و above the letter: short 'u' (بُ = bu)
Kasra ( ِ ) == Slash below the letter: short 'i' (بِ = bi)
Length of a short vowel == One count, never stretched
